senses.gloss:
Jāva
------------------------------------------
Hindu religion and culture started spreading to the various islands of South East Asia even from the first century A. D. Some of the kings of South India who were defeated by their rivals, migrated to the islands like जाव and established their own kingdoms there.
Known as Yavadvīpa, probably from the 10th cent. A. D., जाव was the home of well-known dynasties of kings like Śrīvijaya Rāja.
The work Ajiśaka states that during the first century A. D., twenty thousand people from कलिङ्ग (Orissa, India) came and settled down in the island of जाव.
A very large number of Hindu scriptu-ral works in Sanskrit (excepting the वेदस्) written in the Kawi script have been discovered. The following list can give an idea of the same:
Purāṇas (Mythology):Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa, Viṣṇupurāṇa. Mantraśāstra (Rituals and worship):Sūryasevana (pūjā of शिव and आदित्य); Several mantras connected with ritualistic worship; Mṛtyuñjaya and गायत्री mantras; some hymns like Viṣṇustava. Nītiśāstra (Ethics):Sārasamuccaya of वररुचि, Ādi-purāṇa; Kāmandaka Nītiśāstra. Dharmaśāstra (Social Science):Śivaśāsana; Kuṭāra Mānavāgama; Devāgama; Svarajambu. Vyākaraṇa (Grammar):Ādisvara; Amaramālā; Vṛttasañcaya. Apart from these there is the famous Rāmāyaṇa Kakawin in old Javanese. Works on medicines, अस्त्रोलोग्य्, stories and literary classics and history works have also been found. The Rāmakavaca (22 verses in Sanskrit) appears to be quite popular even now.
Śaivism made its first appearance in जाव around 4th century A. D. The oldest image of गणेश has been found on the Dieng plateau. Another image found near Borobudur is considered to be the finest.
